transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Um... I guess... I just can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll start talking about an overnight shift, and then... I don't know, I end up jumping to soccer. Or... paint colors, or patient charts. 

I can just see everyone getting lost when I talk. So... yeah. That's why.
During the times when your speech becomes harder to follow, have you needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

Um... no. Not really. 

I still sleep. I'm usually pretty tired from work anyway, so... yeah, I haven't noticed anything like that.
When did you first notice yourself starting to jump between topics like this?

Um... a while, I guess. Like... maybe a year and a month? Around there. 

That's when the talking got bad. And... I don't know, it's also when I started feeling like I was being watched all the time. But... yeah. About a year and a month.
When you feel watched, do you believe that someone is actually watching you?

Um... yeah. I mean... I know they are. 

The supervisors at work. They... they changed my shifts around. And I know they watch me on the unit cameras. Just... trying to see if I'm unsafe or something. 

Everyone else tells me it's just staffing shortages, but... I know they're watching me.
Since these beliefs began, have you had a sustained period when your mood was unusually depressed or unusually elevated?

Um... yeah. Mostly just... really down. Depressed. 

It's... I don't know. When I feel the worst, like really low... that's when I'm the most sure about the cameras. That the supervisors are watching me. And... my words just get all tangled up. I can't really explain myself right when it's that bad. So... yeah.
Have there been times when you were not feeling depressed but still believed that your supervisors were watching you?

Um... yeah. There was. 

Like... a few weeks, maybe. I wasn't feeling so... down. But I still knew they were watching. I was still... careful at work. Guarded. Because I knew the cameras were on me.
Was there a continuous period of at least two weeks when you believed you were being watched even though you were not depressed?
Yeah. Like I said... it was a few weeks. I wasn't... I wasn't in that really dark place. But I still knew they were watching. I still had to be careful.
How long did your depressed mood last continuously at its worst?
Um... a long time. It's... the feeling down, and just... not caring about anything... it's been going on for a while. Like... maybe a year and two months? Something like that.
During that period of feeling depressed, did you lose interest or pleasure in most of the things you normally enjoy?

Yeah... I guess so. 

I don't really do much anymore. I used to... I don't know, sketch stuff. Murals. Cook for people. Play soccer sometimes. But... I don't really care about any of that now. It just feels pointless. I usually just stay in my apartment and ignore my phone.
